summary: Defines the Network Control Protocol for setting up and configuring the Xerox Network Systems Internet Datagram Protocol over PPP. It is now historic.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines the PPP control protocol for setting up XNS Internet Datagram Protocol communication. Once the link and XNSCP are open, peers can send XNS IDP datagrams in PPP frames.

questions: what is xns control protocol for ppp
subtitle: Defines how PPP establishes and carries Xerox XNS Internet Datagram Protocol traffic.

tldr.problem: PPP needs a network control protocol to establish and configure XNS Internet Datagram Protocol communication across a point-to-point link.
tldr.mechanism: The peers first configure the link with LCP, then use XNSCP to open XNS IDP; each XNS IDP datagram is carried in one PPP frame.
tldr.outcome: The RFC requires PPP links supporting XNS IDP to carry at least 576 octets in the frame information field. Unit metadata classifies it as Historic.

today: RFC 1764 is classified as Historic in the unit metadata. It specifies the PPP network control protocol for XNS IDP.

sections.title: PPP Link Setup and Network Protocols
sections.content:
PPP carries datagrams for different network-layer protocols over point-to-point links. It uses the Link Control Protocol (LCP) to establish, configure, and test the data link, and uses Network Control Protocols to configure network-layer protocols.

For XNS IDP, the peers first complete LCP setup and then exchange XNSCP packets to select and configure the XNS IDP protocol.
sections.plainLanguage: PPP sets up the link first and then configures the network protocol that will use it. XNSCP handles that second step for XNS IDP.

sections.title: XNSCP Negotiation
sections.content:
XNSCP configures, enables, and disables the XNS IDP protocol modules at both ends. It uses the same packet-exchange mechanism as LCP and uses Configure-Request, Configure-Ack, Configure-Nak, Configure-Reject, Terminate-Request, Terminate-Ack, and Code-Reject.

XNSCP packets must not be exchanged before PPP reaches the Network-Layer Protocol phase. XNSCP defines no configuration options.
sections.plainLanguage: The two peers use XNSCP messages to agree to use XNS IDP. They can begin this exchange only after PPP has finished its earlier link setup.

sections.title: Sending XNS IDP Datagrams
sections.content:
Before sending XNS IDP packets, PPP must reach the Network-Layer Protocol phase and XNSCP must reach the Opened state. A PPP frame uses protocol field 0x0025 for an XNS IDP datagram.

Each frame carries exactly one XNS IDP packet. Since the RFC says there is no standard method to fragment and reassemble these datagrams, a supporting PPP link must allow an information field of at least 576 octets.
sections.plainLanguage: Datagrams can be sent after both PPP and XNSCP are ready. Each frame carries one datagram, so the link must support the stated minimum frame information size.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that security issues are not discussed in this memo. It does not define security protections for XNS IDP datagrams carried over PPP.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo does not discuss security issues.

references.text: Simpson, W., "The Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP)", STD 51, RFC 1661, July 1994.
